Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-12
Time: 16:00 - 16:57 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Recording: https://redwood-recordings.s3/ff/2026-10-12-epk

Summary:
Kickoff for implementation and integration. Main topics: network/VPC peering, SSO/KMS and audit logs, staging vs prod runbooks, pilot performance targets (p99 latency, throughput), model placement (hosted vs dedicated vs private), benchmark plan and next steps for pilot.

Topics:
- Network & peering
- Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, data retention
- Pilot scope & success criteria
- Runtime/perf expectations and KV cache behaviour
- Timeline and immediate action items

Transcript:
[00:00] Jesse (AE): okay hey everyone thanks for joining. I'm Jesse Marshall from Redwood, i'll kick off and then pass to Priya and Hugo. quick soundcheck are we good?
[00:18] Daniel (CTO): yep sounds good on my end.
[00:22] Priya (CSM): thanks all, welcome, we'll keep this to an hour. objective is to align on integration touchpoints and next steps for the pilot.
[01:05] Jesse: great. Everpeak, can you walk us through who owns networking, security and the app side? and what your timeline looks like?
[01:22] Daniel: sure, i'll start. Liam is SRE lead so he'll take networking and infra, Marta owns ml infra and model ops, Sofia is product and will own success criteria. timeline wise we want a pilot in 4 weeks if possible, production in Q1.
[01:45] Marta: just to add, we need auditability for inference requests and full syscall logs for some workflows — as part of our compliance checklist.
[02:10] Jesse: understood. from Redwood side Priya will drive onboarding and runbooks, Hugo the technical integration and benchmark. Hugo, do you want to cover VPC and deployment options?
[02:30] Hugo (SE): yeah quick note — we support three modes: hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved pools) and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). For your compliance needs, Private with customer VPC peering is typically preferred. there are two main patterns: direct peering for low latency, or controlled private link via our partner fabric.
[03:10] Liam (SRE): what's the typical latency impact for peering vs hosted? we have tight p99 targets for some endpoints.
[03:22] Hugo: good question. in our benchmarks, peering into Dedicated gave us p99 in the 70-120ms range for short prompts on A100-like infra; hosted can be a bit variable depending on region and multi-tenant load. for your targets can you quantify p99 SLA?
[03:48] Sofia (PM): target is p99 under 150ms for 512 token prompts for the main chat endpoint. bulk batch jobs can be relaxed.
[04:05] Jesse: that helps. also want to flag automatic prefix caching and KV cache behaviors — that can shave token costs and latency. note sometimes transcripts show kv "cash" in our docs, sorry potato autocorrect — but it's KV cache.
[04:35] Marta: ok KV cash — noted. also, we have encrypted at rest requirements and KMS integration via our cloud HSM. how does Redwood handle key management?
[04:50] Hugo: Redwood Private can integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping and audit logs. we'll need a short security doc exchange and a proof of concept to validate key rotation.
[05:20] Daniel: you mentioned audit logs — we need per-request logs and the ability to store them in our S3 with lifecycle rules.
[05:33] Priya: that's in our standard private deployment checklist — we can push delivery of audit log sinks to your S3, and include log format and fields in the runbook.
[05:50] Jesse: on retention what are you expecting?
[05:55] Daniel: 90 days primary, then archive to cold storage for 7 years for certain regulated flows.
[06:08] Hugo: ok we'll note that as a requirement. it affects storage sizing and cost for the pilot.
[06:25] Sofia: another question — how are we handling model version pinning and rollbacks during the pilot? we can't risk user-facing regressions.
[06:37] Hugo: Redwood has rollout policies: canary and A/B, with automatic fallback to a compatible model. for Private we still surface the same control plane so you can pin versions per route. there is minor config for KV cache invalidation on rollouts.
[07:05] Marta: great. also curious about quantization and perf tradeoffs, we run some Llama 2 variants and want to try int8 on dedips, uh Dedicated?
[07:18] Hugo: yep ded- - Dedicated supports quantized runtimes; note that some attention kernels behave differently on quantized weights which can slightly affect quality — we'll advise per-model. we'll include a small eval checklist to measure degree of divergence on your eval set.
[07:45] Jesse: i'll add that to the next steps.
[08:05] Liam: network details — we use AWS in us-east-1, we have Transit Gateway and strict egress rules. how do we handle firewall rules and whitelisting?
[08:20] Hugo: we can do VPC peering and exchange IP ranges, or use private link which avoids egress. for peering we'll need the peering CIDRs and routing table entries; we'll provide a template.
[08:45] Daniel: timeline to get peering up?
[08:49] Hugo: typically 3-7 business days once both sides open the ticket and approve routes, sometimes longer with transit gateways.
[09:05] Priya: action: we'll send the peering template and network checklist after this meeting.
[09:15] Sofia: on the pilot scope, what counts as success?
[09:20] Jesse: short answer: meet p99 latency target for main route, throughput above X tokens/sec under expected load, and pass the quality eval on your test prompts. also operationally: stable logging and SSO integration.
[09:42] Marta: on SSO — we use Okta with SAML. can Redwood integrate?
[09:48] Hugo: yes SAML SSO is supported, also SCIM for provisioning. for Private we'll integrate with your IdP via secure connector.
[10:05] Daniel: are there specific compliance artifacts we need from you? SOC2 report, pen test summary?
[10:12] Priya: we can share SOC2 Type II, our pen test one-pager and a summary of data flows. we'll redact PII in shared materials.
[10:25] Marta: small ask — can we test the request-level masking / PII redaction in the pilot? we have regulated PII in some prompts.
[10:34] Hugo: yes, we have hooks for pre-processing with redaction or you can deploy a sidecar filter. we'll include an example for the runbook.
[10:50] Jesse: on cost — Dedicated reserved pools are committed; we can show a burn-rate model. Redwood Optimize also has recommendations for batching and cache hints to reduce unit cost.
[11:10] Sofia: helpful, can you share a simple TCO spreadsheet?
[11:15] Jesse: yes, will share.
[11:22] (crosstalk)
[11:35] Marta: small clarification on "streaming responses" — we need partial token streaming to the UI. any caveats?
[11:42] Hugo: streaming is supported. private mode uses the same streaming protocols. one caveat: with batching or very aggressive caching there can be small reordering; we'll include recommended settings for interactive endpoints.
[12:05] Liam: about ingress rate limiting — we have spike patterns from internal tools, can Redwood impose per-route rate limits?
[12:15] Hugo: yes per-route QPS limits, token limits, and backpressure policies. we can also configure burst windows for Dedicated.
[12:30] Daniel: security review: do you support customer-managed keys for logs and for model artifacts?
[12:38] Priya: yes we support KMS integrations for both artifact and log encryption — details will be in the security packet.
[12:55] Jesse: moving a little forward — pilot rollout plan suggestion: 2-week smoke, 2-week full pilot in prod-like staging, then expand. thoughts?
[13:08] Sofia: 4-week total seems doable.
[13:14] Marta: we'll need staging parity especially network and KMS.
[13:20] Jesse: agreed. Hugo will run a pre-prod checklist with your team.
[13:30] Hugo: i'll draft a benchmark script for your model set and share it. it'll include 512/2k token flows, concurrency profiles, and a sample eval set.
[13:50] (silence)
[14:05] Daniel: small question re: data residency — some EU flows must stay in eu-central. can Redwood route regionally?
[14:13] Hugo: yes routing policies allow region pinning; for Private you'd place runtime in the desired region. we'll document region options and latencies.
[14:30] Priya: action: send regional deployment options doc.
[14:38] Jesse: let's talk about integrations — we saw you use Kafka for eventing?
[14:44] Marta: yes we produce inference events to Kafka for observability; need ordering guarantees.
[14:50] Hugo: we can emit events to Kafka, or deliver to S3; we can also provide tracing hooks. note ordering depends on consumer topology. we'll add a recommended pattern.
[15:15] Sofia: can we run a short bench where Redwood calls our staging endpoint to confirm end-to-end?
[15:22] Hugo: yes we'll run an end-to-end test once peering and SSO are configured.
[15:35] (background noise)
[16:05] Jesse: ok quick recap of immediate deliverables — Priya runbook + security packet, Jesse pricing sheet, Hugo benchmark script, customer to share traffic profile and open peering ticket. any other asks?
[16:20] Daniel: please include the audit log schema.
[16:30] Priya: noted.
[16:35] Marta: timeline for the benchmark run?
[16:38] Hugo: target week of 2026-10-19, assuming network & test creds are available.
[16:50] Sofia: ok, and one more on routing: automatic fallback to hosted in case Dedicated capacity exhausted — do we lose pins or data locality?
[16:58] Hugo: good question. fallback maintains API contract; for data locality you'd need to configure region fallback rules. there is some re-routing cost but we preserve model pins.
[17:25] Jesse: i'll note we need to document fallback policy for your security team.
[17:40] Daniel: last item — procurement timeline, we have a vendor review meeting next month. how quickly can we get pricing and support SLAs?
[17:50] Jesse: we'll send pricing and SLA sheet by Oct 15.
[18:02] (several people talking)
[18:20] Priya: closing — we'll follow up with calendar invites for network kickoff and benchmark slot. thanks everyone.
[18:30] Daniel: thanks all.
[18:35] Jesse: thanks, meeting end.
